title: GUIDE-01 Coaching conversation for sales managers
text:
# GUIDE-01 Coaching conversation for sales managers

*PT Nusantara Seluler (fictional). Owner: Head of People Partner (Sales).*

Use this guide when a team member's territory is below expectation on **controllable** drivers.

1. **Start with context, not the number.** Share the adjusted view: what part of the gap was outside their control (outages, competitor promos)?
2. **Look at drivers together.** Active outlets, effective-call rate, stock availability, net adds. Ask which one they believe is the biggest lever.
3. **Agree on 1-3 actions for the next two weeks**, each with a measurable check (e.g. "re-activate 12 priority outlets in Kecamatan X").
4. **Offer support.** Pairing with an experienced colleague, a sharing session with a peer cluster that is above expectation, or a backfill request if the team is short-staffed.
5. **Recognise effort and progress** at the next check-in, even when the target is still not met.

New joiners (tenure < 12 months) benefit most from structured coaching; prioritise them.

title: POL-01 Performance management and use of AI in people processes
text:
# POL-01 Performance management and use of AI in people processes

*PT Nusantara Seluler (fictional). Owner: Head of People Partner (Sales). Version 2026.1. Applies together with the PKB (collective labour agreement).*

## Performance cycle
- Scorecards are reviewed monthly and rated at year end. Results ("what", KPI scorecard) are combined with behaviour ("how", AKHLAK values: Amanah, Kompeten, Harmonis, Loyal, Adaptif, Kolaboratif).
- KPI achievement is capped between 0% and 150% before weighting.
- Comparisons between people are only made within cohorts of similar territories (java_urban, java_rural, outside_java_urban, outside_java_rural, 3t) and using adjusted attainment.

## Consequence management
- Missing targets is a coaching matter first. Formal warnings follow the sequence SP1 -> SP2 -> SP3 and are decided by the line manager with HR, never by a system.
- No termination can be based on target achievement alone; it requires a breach of company regulations or the PKB after the warning sequence.

## Use of AI and people analytics
1. AI may draft coaching notes, development plans, recognition messages and evidence summaries. A manager must review and edit drafts before they are saved or sent.
2. AI must not produce ratings, rankings of individuals, bonus decisions, warning letters or termination recommendations.
3. Team-level people metrics (engagement, attrition, tenure mix) are only shown for groups of 5 or more people; sensitive metrics (engagement) need 5 or more respondents.
4. Individual flight-risk scores are not shown to line managers.
5. Partner (distributor) sales staff are not employees and are not individually assessed; only aggregate capacity and activity are used.
6. Sensitive attributes (health, religion, union membership, ethnicity) are never used.
7. Every AI recommendation that leads to an action is recorded in the audit log with the approving manager.
8. Employees can see the explanation of their own scorecard and adjusted attainment.

title: SOP-01 Revenue gap review and escalation
text:
# SOP-01 Revenue gap review and escalation

*PT Nusantara Seluler (fictional). Owner: Head of Sales Planning & Performance. Version 2026.1.*

## Purpose
Make sure every territory that is behind plan has a named owner, a diagnosed cause and an approved action within one working day.

## Definitions
- **Raw attainment** = actual revenue / target revenue (month-to-date, pro-rata).
- **Expected revenue** = revenue the territory should deliver given its market potential (population, purchasing power, coverage), before non-controllable events.
- **Adjusted attainment** = (actual revenue + estimated loss from non-controllable events) / expected revenue.
- **Non-controllable events**: network outages, natural disasters, competitor price actions. Logged in the shock event register by Network Operations or the Branch Marketing Officer.

## Severity
| Tier | Trigger | Delivery |
|---|---|---|
| P1 | Forecast month-end attainment < 90% **and** a sudden drop (> 30% day-on-day in a desa or kecamatan), or a confirmed event | Immediate message to the responsible owner |
| P2 | MTD attainment > 10 points below pro-rata | Morning digest |
| P3 | Small or slowly developing gaps | Weekly summary |

## Steps
1. **Detect.** The morning job (07:00 WIB) computes MTD attainment and a month-end forecast per cluster and kecamatan.
2. **Route.** Each alert goes only to the role that can act: Sales Supervisor (kecamatan), Cluster Sales Manager (cluster), Branch Manager (branch). Regional General Managers receive the provincial digest and unresolved escalations only.
3. **Clarify.** If the drop may be caused by the network, the owner is asked "Is this caused by a site outage?" before any action is proposed. Network-caused gaps are routed to the Regional Network Operations Manager and excluded from the sales team's controllable gap.
4. **Act.** The owner proposes or approves an action plan (outlet activation, route change, stock replenishment, coaching, backfill request). Plans are approved by the next-level manager.
5. **Escalate.** An unacknowledged P1 escalates once to the next level after 4 working hours, and once more to the Regional General Manager after a further 8 hours. No repeated reminders.
6. **Close.** The alert is resolved when the metric returns to within 5 points of pro-rata, or the gap is reclassified as non-controllable.

## Rules
- Maximum 3 interrupting messages per person per day. No messages during quiet hours (21:00-07:00 local time, Friday 11:30-13:00).
- "Not my territory" responses must be reviewed by Sales Planning within 2 working days to correct ownership data.

title: SOP-02 Outlet activation, NusaPOS adoption and recharge stock
text:
# SOP-02 Outlet activation, NusaPOS adoption and recharge stock

*PT Nusantara Seluler (fictional). Owner: Head of Channel Management. Version 2026.1.*

## Purpose
Keep at least 80% of registered outlets active every month and recharge stock available at 97% of outlet-days or more.

## Responsibilities
- **Channel Officer (cluster):** activation and re-activation of outlets, NusaPOS onboarding, stock monitoring.
- **Sales Supervisor (kecamatan):** plans partner canvasser routes so every outlet is visited per its call cycle.
- **Distributor partner:** employs canvassers and keeps voucher/recharge stock; bound by the partner agreement.
- **Branch Channel Manager:** reviews partner performance monthly.

## Activation playbook (when active outlets fall below 75%)
1. Pull the list of outlets inactive for 30+ days, ranked by last 3-month recharge value.
2. Prioritise the top 10-15 outlets per canvasser per day; plan routes by kecamatan.
3. Check stock: if recharge availability < 95%, raise a replenishment request with the distributor the same day.
4. Pair new canvassers (tenure < 3 months) with an experienced canvasser for the first two weeks.
5. Re-check activation after 7 days; escalate to the Branch Channel Manager if no improvement.

## Call cycle
| Outlet type | Visit frequency |
|---|---|
| konter_pulsa | weekly |
| minimarket | weekly |
| warung | every 2 weeks |
| agen | every 2 weeks |

## Effective call
A visit is an *effective call* when the outlet places an order or completes a NusaPOS transaction during the visit. Target effective-call rate: 70%.

title: SOP-03 Handling revenue impact of network outages
text:
# SOP-03 Handling revenue impact of network outages

*PT Nusantara Seluler (fictional). Owner: Regional Network Operations Manager. Version 2026.1.*

## Purpose
Separate network-caused revenue loss from sales performance so that sales teams are not held accountable for outages they cannot control.

## Steps
1. Network Operations logs every outage longer than 4 hours affecting 5 or more sites in the shock event register, with the affected desa.
2. Revenue Assurance estimates the prepaid revenue lost (baseline daily revenue x outage days x share of traffic lost).
3. The estimated loss is added back when computing **adjusted attainment** for the affected territories and people.
4. The Regional Network Operations Manager is the accountable owner of the recovery; the Cluster Sales Manager supports with customer retention offers after restoration.
5. Repeat outages (3+ in a quarter in the same kecamatan) are escalated to the Regional General Manager for a capex review.

## Service levels
- Site restoration: 4 hours (urban), 12 hours (rural), 48 hours (3T areas).
- Communication to affected outlets within 24 hours.
